walkthroughs.body_html: Hubble sits in low Earth orbit (~540 km). JWST is at the L2 point, ~1.5 million km from Earth, where its sunshield keeps the mirror cold for infrared observation.
Light grasp scales with area, so it scales with aperture squared. JWST's 6.5 m mirror gathers (6.5/2.4)^2 ~ 7.3 times more light than Hubble's 2.4 m mirror.
Bigger apertures give finer detail. Resolution is roughly proportional to wavelength divided by aperture, so larger mirrors see smaller features.
